alive_bonus.citation: Tassa et al. (2018). DeepMind Control Suite. arXiv:1801.00690
alive_bonus.how_used: The alive_bonus (1.0/step) dominates the return and rewards the agent for merely existing briefly before falling. Reducing it shifts the return balance toward forward_velocity, discouraging the stand-and-tip hacking behavior.

forward_velocity_tolerance.citation: Tassa et al. (2018). DeepMind Control Suite. arXiv:1801.00690
forward_velocity_tolerance.how_used: Per Tassa et al. (DM Control Suite), bounded smooth tolerance kernels in [0,1] produce well-scaled gradients and avoid unbounded reward hacking. Replace raw forward_velocity with a tolerance kernel that saturates at a target running speed, keeping the component comparable to the (now reduced) alive_bonus.

forward_weight.citation: Tassa et al. (2018). DeepMind Control Suite. arXiv:1801.00690
forward_weight.how_used: forward_weight=5.0 dominates the return (≈1.0 per step vs 0.1 alive) and incentivizes transient velocity spikes during a fall. Lowering it rebalances the return so that sustained locomotion over many alive steps beats a short dive. Keeps the bounded-unit-reward philosophy of DM Control (arXiv:1801.00690) where no single component dwarfs the others.

tolerance_lower.citation: Tassa et al. (2018). DeepMind Control Suite. arXiv:1801.00690
tolerance_lower.how_used: Current tolerance band [1.0, 4.0] with margin=1.0 means the agent is never in the saturating region (mean_forward_velocity=0.64 < 1.0), so the gradient of the kernel always points to 'go faster now', which a falling hopper can satisfy via a brief forward lurch. Lowering the lower bound to a modest achievable target (e.g., 0.5 m/s) lets a stably-running policy sit inside the flat-1.0 region and removes the marginal incentive to spike velocity at the cost of balance (tolerance_reward_kernel, Tassa et al. 2018).

upright_bonus.citation: Tassa et al. (2018). DeepMind Control Suite. arXiv:1801.00690
upright_bonus.how_used: The diagnosed failure is progressive forward tipping of the torso, but reward_contract.expected_info_keys only exposes x_velocity — no torso height or angle is available. The ideal edit is a bounded tolerance term on torso_angle near 0 (or torso z-height above a threshold), shaped like reward = tolerance(torso_angle, bounds=(-0.2, 0.2), margin=0.2), added with a positive weight. This would directly penalize the tip-over that is currently ending every episode. Adapter needs to surface `torso_angle` (and ideally `z_height`) in info.
